reviews.text: This is True Detective meets Stephen King; missing kids with a hint of the supernatural – but it goes nowhere.
reviews.author: Francesca Steele

reviews.text: The Black Phone might not be consistently terrifying, but it has its moments. Ultimately, it is let down by an undercooked, patchy script and odd stylistic and editing choices that remove well-built tension.
reviews.author: William Stottor

reviews.text: In The Black Telephone some of the director's stylems are observed, such as the prominence of children/adolescents in the action, perverse villains who hide their faces behind peculiar masks, and the presence of pagan or religious elements.
reviews.author: Denise Pieniazek

reviews.text: The Black Phone isn’t just the best film Scott Derrickson has made thus far… it’s a larger testament to the kind of humanity and imagination that can come out of modern horror.
reviews.author: James Preston Poole

reviews.text: The filmmaking team behind “Sinister” (2012), director and co-screenwriter Scott Derrickson, co-screenwriter Robert Cargill and Hawke, reunite for another hit. Think John Irving’s “A Prayer for Owen Meany” except framed in the horror genre.
reviews.author: Sarah Vincent

reviews.text: Based on Joe Hill’s book of the same name, the creators provide one of the most memorable contemporary horrors, discussing loss, domestic violence, supernatural, and much more.
reviews.author: Zofia Wijaszka

reviews.text: It's not groundbreaking, but it's very well done.
reviews.author: Mark Kermode

reviews.text: Here’s one of those supernatural thrillers that would actually be better off without the supernatural elements.
reviews.author: Matt Brunson

reviews.text: Derrickson has succeeded in making a film that is definitely worth any horror fan's time. Is it a new classic? No, but by hell, it is one fun ride.
reviews.author: Emma-Jane Betts

reviews.text: The Black Phone carries a horror premise with a supernatural touch full of potential, but it plays too safe by betting on a narrative that's too simple, predictable, and repetitive.
reviews.author: Manuel São Bento

reviews.text: A New Horror Icon lives
reviews.author: Zach Pope

reviews.text: Ethan Hawke attempts to scare in a straightforward serial killer nightmare that is about as satisfying as a one-minute payphone call.
reviews.author: Ryan Oquiza

reviews.text: Derrickson is comfortable navigating dark and demented worlds, so it's frustrating when "The Black Phone" doesn't come together in a successful way.
reviews.author: Matthew Passantino

reviews.text: Derrickson prioritizes jump-scares and sustaining a disquieting mood over the lives of these kids. He loses himself in the technique when the real nightmare is staring him right in the face.
reviews.author: Rubén Rosario

reviews.text: These additions significantly alter the tone of the original story for better or worse depending on what kind of horror movie you’re looking for.
reviews.author: Jenn Adams

reviews.text: It’s a B-movie abduction flick centered in the 80s that values simplicity over complexity. And ultimately, The Black Phone is a theatrical experience that is sure to get your blood pumping.
reviews.author: Benjamin Wiebe

reviews.text: Scott Derrickson's return to his horror sandbox, The Black Phone, is a fantastic vintage horror film that utilizes sound against its audience.
reviews.author: William Jones

reviews.text: Ethan Hawke continues his spectacular mid-career run in a rare villainous role.
reviews.author: Richard Roeper

reviews.text: The Black Phone is easily one of the best horror/trillers this year. The young cast members Mason Thames and Madeleine McGraw light up ever scene they are in & then Ethan Hawke becomes something horrifically unknown and yet interesting. A MUST WATCH FILM!
reviews.author: Samuel Leggett Jr.

reviews.text: a good ole fashioned scary night out at the movies filled with dead kids, creepy masks, and haunting 8mm film.
reviews.author: Jonathan DeHaan

reviews.text: It is as much ‘coming of age’ as ‘run from the monster’, and that is very much to its credit.
reviews.author: Grant Watson

reviews.text: The Black Phone is a solid, classical horror flick by a team who love the genre and excel at their craft — what more could you ask for?
reviews.author: Travis Johnson

reviews.text: In theory, the concept of The Black Phone is unique and interesting.
reviews.author: Allison Rose

reviews.text: The Black Phone is grounded in realism for a large part of the story & has just a cinch of fictional horror that truly allows the audience to become immersed in the story, which is elevated by good performances & unique creativity within the narrative.
reviews.author: Jason Escamilla

reviews.text: The Black Phone delivers one of the best stories and some of the best characters that I have seen all year. Ethan Hawke's performance as The Grabber paired with Derrickson's directing of Cargill's script are a match made in hell.
reviews.author: Cody Leach

reviews.text: The Black Phone comes with a fairly simple premise, but it’s in the execution where Scott Derrickson reminds us that the real horrors in society can be scarier than ones oftentimes manufactured in the horror genre for cheap, gory thrills.
reviews.author: Paul McGuire Grimes

reviews.text: Though its story is hardly seamless, “The Black Phone” keeps its audience locked in by maintaining its sinister tone and building some true edge-of-your-seat suspense.
reviews.author: Keith Garlington

reviews.text: I was entirely willing to go where this movie wanted to take me… right up until the end, when it decided to sell the creepy message...
reviews.author: Eve Tushnet

reviews.text: “The Black Phone” is a well put together horror-thriller whose ring is worth answering.
reviews.author: Rosa Parra

reviews.text: It works at the moment; combining supernatural elements with a story of survival, and a palpable character arc for its protagonist. Full review in Spanish.
reviews.author: Sebastian Zavala Kahn

reviews.text: Small-scaled horror that relies on atmospheric dread
reviews.author: Jordan Ruimy

reviews.text: The young actors rise above their material, but Hawke is wasted as the killer.
reviews.author: David Stratton

reviews.text: A tight, efficient thriller that kept me engaged from beginning to end.
reviews.author: Sean Chandler

reviews.text: A chilling and quite original horror film, which only takes a few long distance calls to deftly communicate the most unexpected scares of supernatural bill. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Yasser Medina

reviews.text: the supernatural ooga-booga is nicely balanced with the more socially realistic elements, particularly the harsh, Darwinian world of the junior high social strata
reviews.author: James Kendrick

reviews.text: in cinema when an entire plot hinges on a magical doodad and some psychic abilities the complete and total avoidance of their interrogation discombobulates the world and superimposes a sense of falseness to its entirety.
reviews.author: Taylor Baker

reviews.text: Ethan Hawke continues to impress us in an extremely difficult and caustic role.
reviews.author: Don Shanahan

reviews.text: A juicy slice of well-made horror cheese for the undemanding horror fan who relishes being easily frightened. Oh, and The Black Phone easily holds up to a second viewing. Interesting how even when you know a scare is coming, it still scares.
reviews.author: Jim Schembri

reviews.text: The film has real character, and an engrossing sense of time and place, at least until it winds up in the dungeon.
reviews.author: Simon Miraudo

reviews.text: I enjoyed the blend of drama, horror and supernatural.  Such movies can become very formulaic (borrowing heavily from previous works) but this held my attention all the way through.
reviews.author: Matthew Toomey

reviews.text: Much of this feels contrived to distract us from what the film ultimately appears to be about.
reviews.author: Jake Wilson

reviews.text: The atmospheric and unnerving horror movie doesn’t just have literal scares, it effectively taps into our primal fears about menacing predators in all forms.
reviews.author: Wenlei Ma

reviews.text: Hawke does not have much screen time, but his performance as the peevish, sadistic kidnapper -- a man ready to explode into violence at any moment -- makes the Grabber one of the best baddies in recent memory.
reviews.author: John Lui

reviews.text: Dismal basement? Yep! Serial killer with handy van? Yep! Apparitions with axes to grind? What do you think?
reviews.author: Andiee Paviour

reviews.text: The Black Phone doesn't always know when to stay on the line, but the chilling flick is still a horror-movie call worth taking.
reviews.author: Sarah Ward

reviews.text: A well-rounded film that captures our attention, scares and surprises us while making a case for self-defense in times where school abuse was normalized. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Emiliano Basile

reviews.text: Scott Derrickson couples incredibly smart casting with a 70s aesthetic perfect for this horrific take on a ghost story
reviews.author: Ro Moore

reviews.text: At heart this is a well-oiled suspense thriller where angry ghosts provide plot shortcuts, but the horror moments can be genuinely disturbing.
reviews.author: Anthony Morris

reviews.text: Derrickson is restrained with his jump scares and succinct with world-building. The Black Phone subverts any number of Spielbergian tropes — not to mention voguish nostalgia — with a grimy, bad-old-days version of the past.
reviews.author: Tara Brady

reviews.text: The Black Phone proves to be much more complex than I expected, a pleasant surprise that works hard for its audience -- justly rewarding them with a unique horror film.
reviews.author: Micheal Compton

reviews.text: It is efficiently made, occasionally jump-worthy and mostly gets across the screen like it has somewhere to be -- and knows how to get there.
reviews.author: Graeme Tuckett

reviews.text: The Black Phone might have seemed more revolutionary a few years ago, before complex horror came back into vogue. Nevertheless, it’s a polished, spooky story told by a filmmaker back in his comfort zone.
reviews.author: Victoria Luxford

reviews.text: …a focused, tense and utterly engaging horror yarn…
reviews.author: Anthony O'Connor

reviews.text: Overly tame yet also too nasty to want to watch again.
reviews.author: Edwin Arnaudin

reviews.text: A well oiled thrill machine that feels like part of a dying breed.
reviews.author: Mattie Lucas

reviews.text: Hawke is creepy as all heck but too much of this film feels paint-by-numbers.
reviews.author: Bob Grimm

reviews.text: Kind of a mishmash of three different films but two of them I enjoyed very much. Not sure if I needed the supernatural element to play as big of a role as it did but the performances and Derrickson's confidence behind the camera sell every scene.
reviews.author: Jim Laczkowski

reviews.text: It may very well be the scariest movie you've seen in years. Most horror films aren't really that scary but this one will get under your skin.
reviews.author: Paul Salfen

reviews.text: A supernatural thriller in the Stephen King mold with a pure narrative drive that's never dull and often tense and thrilling.
reviews.author: Peter Canavese

reviews.text: a perplexing puzzle that won’t leave you hanging…up. It won’t necessarily have you on the edge of your seat either, but that’s only because The Black Phone is more creepy than it is frightening. It’s more like watching a crime drama with jump scares,
reviews.author: T.J. Callahan

reviews.text: Spooky, creepy, and expertly paced, The Black Phone plays out with a delicious ‘70s vibe
reviews.author: Frank Wilkins

reviews.text: The Black Phone is a slow-burn thrill ride that packs plenty of surprises and great performances.
reviews.author: Jordy Sirkin

reviews.text: Horror fans, 'The Black Phone' is calling you.
reviews.author: Linda Cook

reviews.text: The trailer presents a terrifying tale of a man that dons creepy masks in an effort to hide his identity, intimidate his victims or perhaps both — however, the full narrative is actually far more disturbing.
reviews.author: Sarah Gopaul

reviews.text: It feels fresh, it’s got the eerie sheen you’d want and it hits its emotional beats. Good for summer horror, I’d say!
reviews.author: Cory Woodroof

reviews.text: A tightrope act of a film that utilises silence masterfully and knows never to overstay its welcome.
reviews.author: Peter Gray

reviews.text: It admirably rallies against the notion of childhood nostalgia to pay tribute to the resilience of kids, yet the slight screenplay hits a familiar and repetitive rhythm.
reviews.author: Katherine McLaughlin

reviews.text: The Black Phone quickly reveals its true face: a clumsy thriller that drags its ambitions far beyond its means.
reviews.author: Filipe Freitas

reviews.text: The breakout talents of “The Black Phone” are young Thames and McGraw, as the siblings who are bonded by the supernatural forces helping them, in different ways, to survive and solve the mystery.
reviews.author: Sean P. Means

reviews.text: For much of the movie’s first act, we’re subjected to horrific violence against children, but once the actual child murderer shows up, the brutality comes to an abrupt halt as Finney and The Grabber engage in an increasingly tiresome back and forth.
reviews.author: Joey Keogh

reviews.text: Despite missing a couple obvious big payoffs for the audience there is still plenty here to enjoy from the solid young leads to Ethan Hawke’s villainy and enough ingenuity to keep us equally on edge and smiling.
reviews.author: Erik Childress

reviews.text: Not enough chills, not enough thrills. The plot lacks logic and the background of the key villain is MIA.
reviews.author: Jackie K. Cooper

reviews.text: The Black Phone is not an old-school splatterfest, but it does aim for the grim intensity of a '70s drive-in movie. Fortunately for us, it is better than most of those ever were.
reviews.author: Steve Biodrowski

reviews.text: Its best moments far outstrip its worst ones, though, resulting in a work that feels at once fussily prepared and a bit undercooked, with artistic attention and running time too often feeling misspent.
reviews.author: George Elkind

reviews.text: The Black Phone is well-paced, well-drawn, and gives us a feeling of being drawn into darkness. It fulfills its potential well.
reviews.author: Abbie Bernstein

reviews.text: The effort is appreciated as far as it goes. But it doesn’t matter how enthusiastically you dial if you end up with a bore on the other end of the line.
reviews.author: Noah Berlatsky

reviews.text: Has a few things going for it, but can’t overcome some plot machinations that don’t quite add up, as well as other elements that aren’t quite developed.
reviews.author: Stephen Silver

reviews.text: A surprisingly audience friendly take on a child murderer, the best parts of this film are Hawke's performance, the visualization of the calls and the mask. Overall, though, this pales in comparison to The Boy Behind The Door. It's surprisingly safe.
reviews.author: Joe Lipsett

reviews.text: There are very few classic hallmarks of horror films in The Black Phone. They arrive in the third act, but before that, it is a lot of… nothing. Talking. No cat-and-mouse chasing. No killing. Not even any suspense.
reviews.author: Alyse Wax

reviews.text: The Black Phone is not a great horror film, but it is a well crafted one that does not insult your intelligence. It does not aim high, but it hits its mark to deliver a compelling and disturbing tale.
reviews.author: Beth Accomando

reviews.text: A pretty enjoyable supernatural thriller.
reviews.author: Tony Baker

reviews.text: A solid little horror flick that will definitely amuse and captivate most while they’re watching it.
reviews.author: Nick Johnston

reviews.text: A limited location, a restricted number of characters and a narrative model rooted in sparseness all demand finesse in order to be spun into feature-length cinema, and The Black Phone shows why, for worse more often than for better.
reviews.author: Charles Bramesco

reviews.text: Possibly the most audience-friendly film about a child murderer that you'll ever see. It plays things a bit too safe, but Derrickson still manages to eke out a few effective moments here and there.
reviews.author: Trace Thurman

reviews.text: It's a terrifyingly tense race-against-time tale that delivers potent scares and contains spot-on performances from Thames (on his debut) and McGraw.
reviews.author: Jeremy Aspinall

reviews.text: A horror movie as rote, low-impact vapor...
reviews.author: Jeffrey Zhang

reviews.text: The Black Phone doesn’t feel like it’s about much more than the admittedly unnerving feeling of entrapment, or the sheer fear of being a kid captured by a maniac. Above all, it’s a memorable piece of retro visuals.
reviews.author: Alci Rengifo

reviews.text: The Black Phone could easily have been excessively nasty but isn’t, and has the slightly surreal quality of a Brothers Grimm fairy tale, though it resolves itself with unseemly haste.
reviews.author: Paul Whitington

reviews.text: Director Scott Derrickson spends time deepening the characters and feelings, rather than making the film either suspenseful or scary. But it's infused with properly unsettling menace.
reviews.author: Rich Cline

reviews.text: The Grabber is supposed to be a magician, but the real sleight-of-hand is from Derrickson... The Black Phone makes quotidian rage more horrifying than the stuff of nightmares.
reviews.author: Peter Howell

reviews.text: The Black Phone isn’t quite the home run I was hoping for, but it’s a very well made and effective thriller.
reviews.author: Maria Lattila

reviews.text: A serial killer thriller / supernatural ghost tale that features impressive performances, is genuinely scary, and is translated well to the screen.
reviews.author: Louisa Moore

reviews.text: This is a movie meant for kids to encounter, enjoy, and hail as a cult classic in 20 years.
reviews.author: Robert Daniels

reviews.text: So tightly-built that it's deliciously watchable even despite how utterly vicious and draining its content is.
reviews.author: Tim Brayton

reviews.text: With a mysterious performance from Ethan Hawke and a pair of child actors, Scott Derrickson has crafted a gut wrenching and high tension inducing thriller with The Black Phone.
reviews.author: Leo Brady

reviews.text: [A] film that would be right at home as part of a drive-in double feature while also feeling thoroughly modern...a combination of old and new school that largely mines the best of both worlds, creating something new, yet still hauntingly familiar.
reviews.author: Allen Adams

reviews.text: 'The Black Phone' is the best Hollywood horror flick since 'Malignant.'
reviews.author: Scott Mendelson

reviews.text: Director Scott Derrickson returns to his horror-drama roots with The Black Phone, a solid, spooky period chiller.
reviews.author: Wendy Ide

reviews.text: The Black Phone feels like it’s trying to reconcile typical horror elements with the more expressive and tender story Derrickson clearly wants to tell. The reconciliation never really comes, but the cast gets us there anyway.
reviews.author: Bilge Ebiri

reviews.text: The Black Phone works effectively with a small cast, two of whom -- Thames and McGraw -- are exceptional child actors. Hawke manages to bring a lot of personality to his unbalanced character despite wearing the mask.
reviews.author: James Berardinelli

reviews.text: The film's marriage of real-life and supernatural horror clashes more than it complements
reviews.author: Prabhjot Bains

reviews.text: It’s scary, intense, and moody. Derrickson’s first film since Doctor Strange is one of the best horror films in a very long time.
reviews.author: Bobby LePire

reviews.text: The Black Phone is a spooky, scary Horror movie with a capital “H” that did everything to remind me why I love a good fright.
reviews.author: Lindsay Traves

reviews.text: For all its atmosphere and scares, The Black Phone is a sweet and tender coming-of-age story, cunningly disguised as something far more sinister.
reviews.author: Joel Harley

reviews.text: Derrickson has a mostly deft touch with The Black Phone. Crucially, he gets you to worry deeply for Finney even if you’re pretty confident he’ll find a way to put The Grabber in his rearview mirror.
reviews.author: Mark Meszoros

reviews.text: The Black Phone is a tightrope act -- alternately thrilling and tender, and the reason it works so well despite these tonal disparities is because of how full its heart is.
reviews.author: Gayle Sequeira

reviews.text: Despite some inspired shots, and jump scares that will have you tossing your popcorn in the air, lackluster teen acting and silly lapses in plausibility undermine an otherwise intriguing idea. This is one incoming call that simply can't find a connection.
reviews.author: Larry Carroll

reviews.text: Taken as a horror film, The Black Phone could underwhelm as it’s mostly light on scares, but it’s far more effective when viewed as a crime thriller. Through this lens, Derrickson has crafted a very unsettling chiller
reviews.author: Rhys Bowen Jones

reviews.text: The Black Phone has some solid set pieces and decent performances from the child leads, but it never quite musters enough substance to horrify in the way that it should.
reviews.author: Natasha Alvar

reviews.text: ...somewhat hit-and-miss...
reviews.author: David Nusair

reviews.text: With a breakthrough performance from Madeleine McGraw and Ethan Hawke’s hauntingly memorable turn as The Grabber, The Black Phone is a solid, pulse-racing horror film that packs a punch, but simply won’t be as delectable on repeat viewings.
reviews.author: Chris Sawin

reviews.text: "There are scarier movies with scarier villains, sturdier logic, and arguably even better filmmaking. But the specific alchemy that makes up The Black Phone means you’d be hard-pressed to find anything else as effective."
reviews.author: Eric Francisco

reviews.text: The Black Phone is an extremely potent kidnapping thriller, with great 70s atmosphere, a creepy score, shouldered by director Scott Derickson's unique touch.
reviews.author: Lee McCoy

reviews.text: This tense horror movie seems a little tentative about how far to go with its subject of child kidnapping/murder, but it still delivers genuinely brutal tension via its vivid characters.
reviews.author: Jeffrey M. Anderson

reviews.text: More psychological than knife hacking but the dark setting and that mask makes this a frightening initiation ritual for teen boys to overcome.
reviews.author: Victoria Alexander

reviews.text: The young cast is terrific and Ethan Hawke is menacing in the horror-thriller that pays tribute to the master Stephen King.  One of the best films of the year.
reviews.author: Joe Friar

reviews.text: Ethan Hawke is absolutely terrifying in this effective thriller that creates a disturbing and nail-biting atmosphere. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Rene Sanchez

reviews.text: Derrickson and his trusty screenwriter, C. Robert Cargill, have the goods to make a sturdy film that smoothly navigates a familiar territory for a savvy horror audience.
reviews.author: James Clay

reviews.text: Though it may not be scary enough for seasoned horror fans, The Black Phone is an intelligent and thoughtful story that is well worth a trip to the cinema this summer.
reviews.author: Rachel West

reviews.text: Great summer horror fun. A 100 minutes of sharp atmosphere and tension, with some laughs. Another solid outing for director Scott Derrickson. Ethan Hawke is great, while Mason Thames and Madeleine McGraw are wonderful. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fico Cangiano

reviews.text: Another real relic from the past uses balloons, baseball and bullies to ring in an occasionally disturbing supernatural thriller with some good adolescent performances and the legitimately scary Ethan Hawke.
reviews.author: John Urbancich

reviews.text: Directed with skillful misdirection and splendid attention to details that resonate with the macabre, it’s a perfect waking nightmare.
reviews.author: Andrea Chase

reviews.text: A film set in 1978 that feels like it was made in 1978 in all the best possible ways... There's a raw realism to it in a supernatural setting that I found really compelling.
reviews.author: Christy Lemire

reviews.text: I feel like I'd seen this a million times before, quite frankly.
reviews.author: Andy Klein

reviews.text: Check out The Black Phone and have a great time with a summer horror with heart and chills!
reviews.author: Rachel Wagner

reviews.text: Unnerving and visceral, this is a clever take on the hostage film.
reviews.author: Kevin Carr

reviews.text: While little here should resonate after a few weeks, the young cast and Hawke work like gangbusters to administer a few legit JUMP scares throughout to keep the audience honest and ready to be shocked.
reviews.author: Dan Buffa

reviews.text: It should be hugely tasteless, and at times it veers perilously close... But it’s saved at every beat by a fearless junior cast and by Derrickson’s commitment to the darker implications of the subject matter.
reviews.author: Kevin Maher

reviews.text: Blessed with a powerful premise that repeatedly gives goosebumps. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ruben Peralta Rigaud

reviews.text: [It] falls short of true terror and white-knuckle suspense, as if Derrickson really did phone it in.
reviews.author: Dann Gire

reviews.text: A film that starts rattling your nerves within the first few minutes and never stops until the end credits begin to roll.
reviews.author: Mike McGranaghan

reviews.text: Frustratingly, potential is all Derrickson’s movie has, as it’s stymied by poor scripting and awkward execution.
reviews.author: Abby Olcese

reviews.text: The siblings are some sort of Hansel and Gretel... With them, Derrickson moves through a forest of missing children and the fears that permeate a society that sweeps dirt under the rug. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Elsa Fernández-Santos

reviews.text: Jump scares, a couple of attempts at humor, and intermittent helpings of Hawke can't quite push the movie over the top.
reviews.author: Robert Denerstein

reviews.text:
The ending involves a “reveal” that is the absolute dumbest thing I’ve heard in years, and I just saw “Jurassic World: Dominion.” It is a boring, ugly, stupid film that I regret having seen.

Other than that, A+.
reviews.author: Ryan Syrek

reviews.text: The Black Phone manages to preserve everything that made Hill’s short story so creepy and undermine it at the same time.
reviews.author: Katie Rife

reviews.text: The film exceeds mediocrity, but the story made it overall a good short film. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Hugo Hernández Valdivia

reviews.text: Movie is thoroughly enjoyable, edge-of-your-seat thriller that will enthrall you from start to finish thanks to great storytelling and well-rounded characters. Ethan Hawke is absolutely terrifying behind the two-piece mask. The young actors deliver too.
reviews.author: Lupe Rodriguez Haas

reviews.text: Part Stranger Things, part The Lovely Bones, and part that urban myth that freaked you out when you were little, The Black Phone is a deliciously creepy throwback anchored by strong performances from both kids and adults alike.
reviews.author: Chris Knight

reviews.text: The Black Phone is a neat dial-back to the indelible sound and style of the 1970s, but as a quirky bit of horror it’s all posture without much bite.
reviews.author: Tom Meek

reviews.text: What distinguishes The Black Phone from its contemporary genre peers, and what situates it as an engaging work of popcorn horror, is that Derrickson seems to actually want his movie to be fun.
reviews.author: Molly Adams

reviews.text: Derrickson executes the film with an atmosphere reminiscent of John Carpenter 's Halloween.  [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Sergio López Aguirre

reviews.text: A quality scare film, with a few jump scares, yes, but more importantly, it instills in us a sense of sustained dread that is necessary to sell this tale.
reviews.author: Steven Prokopy

reviews.text: 'Black Phone' gambles with real-life sordid crimes such as kidnapping and child abuse, but it wins even when it throws in supernatural elements. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jorge Loser

reviews.text: The Black Phone is an amazing achievement in horror cinema...Definitely a must-see.
reviews.author: Damond Fudge

reviews.text: The pair of young leads playing siblings, Thames and McGraw, who take the moody atmospherics of Derrickson's grotty '70s nightmare, and turn it into something that feels considerably more lived in and compelling.
reviews.author: Piers Marchant

reviews.text: The starkly scary, Ethan Hawke-starring chiller 'The Black Phone' packs a more potent-than-expected punch.
reviews.author: André Hereford

reviews.text: This is a fun, fast-paced little malevolent gem that seductively builds to a slam-bang climax that elicited a bevy of hearty cheers from my preview audience. Better, it deserved them.
reviews.author: Sara Michelle Fetters

reviews.text: The Black Phone’s a genuinely frightening film that relies less on jump scares – although there’s a decent amount of those – and more on the truly horrifying, believable threat of a sadistic killer who targets kids.
reviews.author: Rebecca Murray

reviews.text: This film knows that even with its masks, ghosts, and clever jump scares, all the horrors you really need to understand are etched on the faces of the children reacting to the awful adults terrorizing them.
reviews.author: Jeff York

reviews.text: Combining familiar horror tropes with throwback visual flourishes, this mildly unsettling thriller yields some haunting imagery without delivering many genuine frights.
reviews.author: Todd Jorgenson

reviews.text: The Black Phone never unnerves viewers as it should.
reviews.author: Matt Conway

reviews.text: What we're left with is a shallowly dug exploration of murder and mayhem...as if Stranger Danger and Stephen King have taught us nothing but mundane homage.
reviews.author: Kristy Puchko

reviews.text: ‘The Black Phone’ is a dark film, no doubt, but within its sinister plot that reeks of dead bodies, abduction and child abuse, also lies hope for life. This fine balance makes this horror thriller a must-watch
reviews.author: Ronak Kotecha

reviews.text: The Black Phone is a scary, smart, and sublime film that will chill you to the bone, with “The Grabber” joining the ranks of Jason, Michael Myers, and Leatherface as one of horror’s all-time greats.
reviews.author: Matt Rodriguez

reviews.text: 'The Black Phone’ is a dialed-in horror flick.
reviews.author: Jeff Mitchell

reviews.text: [Derrickson] keeps this bowling along quite watchably (apart from the bit when the young woman in front of me buried her face in her boyfriend's arm) and has the good sense to keep it fairly succinct.
reviews.author: Brian Viner

reviews.text: The film’s like the phone. It shouldn’t work, but it does.
reviews.author: Charlotte O'Sullivan

reviews.text: Hawke could have something of a revival on the horizon, one entirely devoted to outright villainy.
reviews.author: Andrea Thompson

reviews.text: This incredibly dark kiddie kidnap horror film hits different with a hard-R rating. It goes for the jugular with a surprising extremity of violence, plus a tone that wobbles between the bleak and the buffoonish.
reviews.author: Katie Walsh

reviews.text: One of the best horror films of 2022
reviews.author: Norman Gidney

reviews.text: Director and co-writer Scott Derrickson has created a horror experience that builds tension superbly well, anchored by fine performances with talented, young leads portrayed by Mason Thames and Madeleine McGraw.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Harris

reviews.text: A tedious, contrived and undercooked amalgam of crime thriller, sci-fi, drama and horror.
reviews.author: Avi Offer

reviews.text: Don't hang up on this effective chiller.
reviews.author: Nate Adams

reviews.text: The Black Phone delivers its quota of thrills while establishing empathy for its bullied and battered youngsters. It’s horror with a heart.
reviews.author: Nathaniel Bell

reviews.text: Everything comes together in a sufficiently nail-biting climax, the kind that expertly builds itself up with both anxiety and excitement.
reviews.author: Nicolás Delgadillo

reviews.text: [Scott Derrickson] proves he can deliver an effective jumpscare -- slick, and not too telegraphed. But there’s a thematic weight here that elevates The Black Phone above any of his previous work in the genre.
reviews.author: Clarisse Loughrey

reviews.text: For such a basic abduction premise, there are a lot of moving parts and details that either don’t go anywhere or lead to a whimper of a payoff.
reviews.author: Radheyan Simonpillai

reviews.text: The Black Phone doesn’t disappoint, at least not so much as it delivers in ways unexpected.
reviews.author: Thom Ernst

reviews.text: Director Scott Derrickson delivers an engaging and genuine thriller that is powered by fantastic child actors, a grounded sense of time and place, and a well-strung thread of unsettling horror.
reviews.author: Rob Dean

reviews.text: The Black Phone is an efficiently told horror story of captivity, dread and friendship. It is an unsettling horror thriller that doesn’t rely on gore, just heaps of tension, suspense and fright that doesn’t rely on a supernatural entity to terrify
reviews.author: Richard Crouse

reviews.text: Basic plot mechanics often don't add up in the details, but high-voltage jump scares abound, and several baroquely composed frames are genuine nightmare fodder.
reviews.author: Leah Greenblatt

reviews.text: I always like being surprised -- especially in this genre.
reviews.author: Jeremy Jahns

reviews.text: The Black Phone is an enjoyable watch, for sure, but it lacks a certain agility, which keeps it from being as great as we want it to be.
reviews.author: Sarah-Tai Black

reviews.text: Nearly everything about “The Black Phone” is perfectly pitched and realized. The compelling storyline is authentically scary, but the emotional connection to Finney and Gwen’s plight gets under your skin.
reviews.author: Jonathan W. Hickman

reviews.text: The film is partly based on Derrickson’s own experiences growing up and it admirably rallies against the notion of childhood nostalgia to pay tribute to the resilience of kids, yet the slight screenplay hits a familiar and repetitive rhythm.
reviews.author: Rachael Harper

reviews.text: Well-acted & structured, and an effective thriller & horror movie. As good a movie as I've seen all summer.
reviews.author: Dan Murrell

reviews.text: It's a fairly gripping and certainly imaginative offering, grounded by the best kid characters and related performances in a horror flick in a long time.
reviews.author: Jim Judy

reviews.text: The Black Phone is a definite winner.
reviews.author: J Hurtado

reviews.text: The deep fear isn’t from ghosts, though they are part of the equation. This is a horror movie borne from fear of the unknown – of Finney’s fate, of the barely restrained rage of The Grabber, of the unseen but very tangible torture of the murdered kids.
reviews.author: MontiLee Stormer

reviews.text: It's been a long time since the genre's seen such a complex and grown-up movie such as The Black Phone, one that doesn't lose their protagonists to cynicism or reduce them to a caricature, one that doesn't rely in gimmicks. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Paula Vázquez Prieto

reviews.text: The Black Phone thrives when its grounded scares have you on the edge of your seat. The supernatural elements do not fully come together, but there is more than enough to creep audiences out.
reviews.author: Austin Burke

reviews.text: The performances are strong, and the film excels in isolated setpieces. It’s just a shame to see a neat idea largely go to waste.
reviews.author: Clint Worthington

reviews.text: Mason Thames and Madeline McGraw beautifully execute emotionally wrought material. Ethan Hawke, may have been a bit under utilize, but is a bone-chilling as they come  grasps the mental complexity and warped child like sensibility of a psychopath
reviews.author: Carla Renata

reviews.text: On the page, The Black Phone is ruthlessly efficient -- a lean, mean, 30-page survival yarn, King-ish mostly in its punchy prose. But in expanding this short story into a feature-length movie, Derrickson fatally slackens the tension.
reviews.author: A.A. Dowd

reviews.text: There is no room for an explanation of why he does what he does — a fact left out that makes it even more chilling to watch. You don’t know what he will do next.
reviews.author: Catalina Combs

reviews.text: The Black Phone is a good piece of trashy summer fun and a great return to his pure horror roots for Derrickson, though it ultimately can’t match the suprise and ingenuity of Sinister.
reviews.author: Jennifer Heaton

reviews.text: This is an Amblin adventure drenched in R-rated fear.
reviews.author: Richard Whittaker

reviews.text: The Black Phone is at turns breathless, terrifying and crowd-pleasing, but always feels authentic to a time when the streets were prowled by real life boogeymen, whose legends were bolstered by the children who whispered their names.
reviews.author: Adam Graham

reviews.text: ... Mixes terror, suspense, fantasy and the unexplainable, a combo that reaps in good results. Just don't ask The Black Phone to muster too much logic because it just can't have it all. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Pablo O. Scholz

reviews.text: Overall, it more than holds our attention, even if we often want to look away.
reviews.author: Christopher Llewellyn Reed

reviews.text: As dark as the story gets, there’s a spring in this film’s step, allowing it to work as an entertaining horror effort, complete with an already killer look for a marque villain.
reviews.author: Aaron Neuwirth

reviews.text: This chilling dip into a horrific suburbia disturbia is a heart-pounding slice of childhood trauma drama built on a troubling foundation of hometown terrors.
reviews.author: Neil Pond

reviews.text: The Black Phone is a chilling horror-thriller with a creepy performance from Ethan Hawke - packaged in a convoluted supernatural serial killer story.
reviews.author: Ben Kendrick

reviews.text: If you thought Ethan Hawke was creepy as cult leader Arthur Harrow in Marvel’s Moon Knight, you ain’t seen nothin’ like what he does in The Black Phone.
reviews.author: Travis Hopson

reviews.text: [The] film isn't much more than a dark and disturbing game, but the filmmaker plays it so well that there's little reason to care about the film doing much more.
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: Underpinned by emotional performances across the board and a commanding atmosphere, The Black Phone aces its foundational qualities and allows its nuances to take control.
reviews.author: Peyton Robinson

reviews.text: The Black Phone doesn’t just dial up paedo-revenge thrills as instantly dubious entertainment, but then devises cack-handed solutions to every last puzzle it sets.
reviews.author: Tim Robey

reviews.text: “The Black Phone” feels unavoidably derivative. But the young actors are appealing, the setting is fondly imagined and the anxieties of adolescence are front and center.
reviews.author: Jeannette Catsoulis

reviews.text: Grimly efficient but more unsettling than scary,...“The Black Phone” hardly breaks new ground in the genre, but it’s reasonably clever and generates a few serious jump-cut shudders.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: Quite an effective thriller that manages to be more retro than "heightened."
reviews.author: Edward Douglas

reviews.text: There’s nothing unheard of here: a bad guy, a haunted house, a hero. But it’s what “The Black Phone” does with those simple parts that sparks a spooky connection.
reviews.author: Michael O'Sullivan

reviews.text: …a classy, often funny thriller that takes edgy, disturbing material and fashions a scare-story for the ages unlike anything we’ve quite seen before...
reviews.author: Eddie Harrison

reviews.text: The narrative is unadventurous, and anyone looking for any neat twists will be disappointed, but the performances are strong – Hawke will leave you in no doubt of his flair for villainy.
reviews.author: Dan Jolin

reviews.text: A pleasant surprise – mixed with relief – to find it being a simple classic horror story, without much fuss, or deep messages to analyze. Full review in Spanish
reviews.author: Jorge Rivera Rubio

reviews.text: The movie made me work… made me feel… made me thrilled. I don’t know what more you could ask of a genre film.
reviews.author: David Poland

reviews.text: We've never seen Ethan Hawke this creepy before. The mask he wears in The Black Phone is very effective and will no doubt be a great Halloween costume this year.
reviews.author: Korey Coleman

reviews.text: It’s not a film that will leave you shaken to the core, but it reminds us that it’s fun to be scared.
reviews.author: Brian Eggert

reviews.text: Ethan Hawke's serial killer enters pantheon of creepy film monsters.
reviews.author: Christian Toto

reviews.text: Despite never playing a villain before (unless you count his loathsome character in Reality Bites), Hawke really makes a meal of his role.
reviews.author: Gena Radcliffe

reviews.text: Scott Derrickson and C. Robert Cargill are adept enough at setting up rich, evocative horror concepts, but they don’t always know what to do with them once they’re in place.
reviews.author: Keith Watson

reviews.text: Derrickson's latest effort isn't as outright horrifying as some of his previous horror entries, but The Black Phone represents a huge step forward in the mastery of his craft. He weaves a haunting tale that leaves a long-lasting impression.
reviews.author: Charlie Ridgely

reviews.text: This is beyond dull, it’s sleep inducing.
reviews.author: Mick LaSalle

reviews.text: At this stage in the parlour game, hardened horror fans may think the jig must be up for Blumhouse but The Black Phone's mix of shocks, gore and family drama has a lot going for it.
reviews.author: Alan Corr

reviews.text: A nasty blast, building to a rousing finale; Ethan Hawke is slimy, ghoulish, and terrific, but Mason Thames is an outstanding find that matches the veteran actor every step in this vicious pleasure
reviews.author: Robert Kojder

reviews.text: Derrickson and Cargill know how to unsettle and frighten their audience and they have succeeded once again with The Black Phone.
reviews.author: Shannon McGrew

reviews.text: It’s a Twilight Zone concept, but Derrickson knows what he’s doing, and you can’t help but feel that swollen bell ringing in the base of your spine.
reviews.author: Jason Shawhan

reviews.text: Then there is Hawke, playing the first truly evil character in his career and bringing to it the kind of nuance and complexity that is a staple of his work.
reviews.author: Don Kaye

reviews.text: What makes The Black Phone stand out is how it perfectly captures what growing up was like in the often raw ’70s and an utter respect for the world of kids. Every adult is either dismissive and distant -- or downright murderous.
reviews.author: Mark Kennedy

reviews.text: A perfect thriller... so engaging that frights revealed in the trailer still won’t be seen coming... lingers long after the lights come up in the best possible way.
reviews.author: Kevin A. Ranson

reviews.text: Derrickson handles the tension with a metronome... and ends up shaping up not only a great villain and future Halloween costume / Funko Pop, but a great horror film that should be at the zenith of the genre in 2022. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Alejandro G. Calvo

reviews.text: An utterly terrifying and sharp-witted horror/thriller that puts us in the shoes of a child serial killer's latest would-be victim.
reviews.author: Christopher Lloyd

reviews.text: The Black Phone is creepy, and The Grabber will make you shrink back in your seat every time he shows up.
reviews.author: DarkSkyLady

reviews.text: If parts of the film can be effective, they are undone by a gleeful desire to depict cruelty, juxtaposed with borderline hilarious plot holes.
reviews.author: Alan Zilberman

reviews.text: Naïf and turbulent, 'Black Phone' offers predictable (and enjoyable) Bogeyman scares and vestiges of genuine teenage angst, capable of disturbing any adult who hasn't reconciled with their past. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Antonio Trashorras

reviews.text: “The Black Phone” has a few sharper points of potential, but Derrickson and co-writer Cargill don't have enough here to bring this supernatural story to a full boil.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: [T]errifying, thrilling, and delivering an ending you won't forget
reviews.author: Corey Chichizola

reviews.text: "The Black Phone" still gets by on the strength of its dark atmosphere and some heart-stopping jump scares, but it's the against-type, blood-curdling performance from Ethan Hawke that makes the film stand out.
reviews.author: Matt Neglia

reviews.text: Resonates as a fable about innocence and violation, strength and maturation, and the way in which the sins of the father either empower or corrupt.
reviews.author: Nick Schager

reviews.text: The Black Phone is dark, to be sure, but still finds room for some hope, and that, along with the acting, makes it a cut above.
reviews.author: Joey Magidson

reviews.text: Hawke, whose creepy bad-guy potential is a plausible new career direction, is unnerving, and there are really good performances from Thames and McGraw.
reviews.author: Peter Bradshaw

reviews.text: The call of “The Black Phone” is one you’ll want to answer.
reviews.author: Bill Goodykoontz

reviews.text: Scott Derrickson fails to connect the important dots—or at least answer some vital questions—that would make this serial killer/ghost story truly haunting.
reviews.author: Todd Gilchrist

reviews.text: A nightmarish scenario packed with very effective scares, but the film's most remarkable quality is that it's also a rather inspiring display of what the youngest of heroes can do to combat the most horrific of monsters.
reviews.author: Perri Nemiroff

reviews.text: Despite its darker-than-dark premise — Abduction! Dead kids! Imprisonment! — The Black Phone finds hope in the midst of the horror. Looking for soulful scares this summer? Answer the call.
reviews.author: Ben Travis

reviews.text:
... It reaches a disquieting tone and a tension that never lets up. 
Mission accomplished, at least in the most basic and essential terrain for any horror film. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Diego Batlle

reviews.text: So much for the missed opportunity that The Black Phone could have been a great horror thriller.
reviews.author: Casey Chong

reviews.text: Black Phone is a solvent story, however routine and self limiting.  It lacks intuition. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Alberto Corona

reviews.text: Stranger Things turns out to be an instructive comparison; in its own way, The Black Phone is just as synthetic, and a lot less fun.
reviews.author: Jesse Hassenger

reviews.text: The message of this inert film – the type that immediately ceases to exist as soon as you walk out of the cinema – is that kids should have self-belief, or something. If that sounds a little thin, you would be correct: this phone rings hollow.
reviews.author: Steph Green

reviews.text: The Black Phone lands in uncanny valley—somewhere between an intelligent thriller that stays with you and a disposable summer entertainment built around jump scares.
reviews.author: John Fink

reviews.text: Tense and unflinching, this is a visceral experience made heart-pounding by a terrifying central performance from Ethan Hawke. Derrickson & Cargill's script makes the most of Joe Hill's horror, and the film will delight and disturb in equal measure.
reviews.author: Daniel Goodwin

reviews.text: The Black Phone is a captivating, terrifying tale that captures real life horrors and trauma and molds them into a horrific thrill ride.
reviews.author: David Gonzalez

reviews.text: Smells like teen spirits...
reviews.author: Anton Bitel

reviews.text: “The Black Phone” carries you along on its own terms — that is, if you accept that it’s less an ingenious freak-out of a thriller than a kind of stylized contraption.
reviews.author: Owen Gleiberman

reviews.text: Peppered with some perfectly executed jump scares, The Black Phone is the perfect film to see in a dark room full of strangers.
reviews.author: Kat Hughes

reviews.text: 'The Black Phone' might be a standard enough horror, but Hawke's performance is anything but and just about saves it from forgettable mediocrity.
reviews.author: Brian Lloyd

reviews.text: Mostly thrills, thanks partly to its strong ensemble cast and some uniform below-the-line excellence from the teams behind production designer Patti Podesta and sound designers Aidin Ashoori and D. Chris Smith.
reviews.author: Simon Abrams

reviews.text: The supernatural horror movie The Black Phone leans more into mounting tension and haunting melancholy rather than outright scares.
reviews.author: Sam Stone

reviews.text: Creepy and suspenseful, The Black Phone has the ghosts of murdered children as story catalysts, but the movie’s equally harrowing moments are in depicting realistic child abuse that can come from a stranger, a family member, or a schoolmate.
reviews.author: Carla Hay

reviews.text: The two put-upon youths and the drama of their lives grip your attention even before THE BLACK PHONE gets to the scary meat of its story.
reviews.author: Michael Gingold

reviews.text: Deliberately paced and restrained with its infrequent yet perfectly placed scares, The Black Phone is primarily a character piece, and Derrickson has assembled an impressive ensemble of child performers.
reviews.author: James Marsh

reviews.text: Closer to Poe than to the subpar American haunted house terror fare of recent years, Derrickson elevates The Black Phone into an effective (very effective) horror film. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Erick Estrada

reviews.text: The Black Phone is as horrifying as Sinister through different means and stars Ethan Hawke in a phenomenally despicable role.
reviews.author: Matt Donato

reviews.text: An airtight film that fully immerses you in the traumatic experience of a child who has been kidnapped. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Mikel Zorrilla

reviews.text: A really terrific coming-of-age horror film with superb work by the young leads.
reviews.author: Chris Bumbray

reviews.text: It is a highly entertaining and gripping thriller of the best kind, one where the horrors of everyday life are not all that easy to escape.
reviews.author: Pete Hammond

reviews.text: You'll care for the characters and best of all, it respects the audience...The Black Phone is stirring and thoroughly captivating.
reviews.author: Jeff Nelson

reviews.text: The Black Phone, C. Robert Cargill and Scott Derrickson's clear sister to Sinister, has managed to exceed extremely high expectations in nearly every aspect.
reviews.author: Amelia Emberwing

reviews.text: Rewards us with a spine-tingling third act.
reviews.author: Dennis Schwartz

reviews.text: Hawke gives a wholly transformative, bloodcurdling, and captivating performance in The Black Phone that is truly unlike anything we've ever seen from him before.
reviews.author: Heather Wixson

reviews.text: It delivers an enjoyably grisly finale that makes you feel like a kid again, for better or worse.
reviews.author: Stephen Saito

reviews.text: The first feature adaptation of Joe Hill's work that demands more big-screen Joe Hill adaptations. Hopefully, Hollywood answers that call.
reviews.author: Eric Vespe

reviews.text: There's much in "The Black Phone" to admire, but even the most patient audience may find themselves frustrated waiting for these pieces to snap into place.
reviews.author: Jason Bailey

reviews.text: Derrickson and Cargill revive the same traits and structure of Sinister to transform Joe Hill's short into a feature-length nightmare full of ghostly kids, violence, scares, and a trio of unforgettable performances.
reviews.author: Meagan Navarro

reviews.text: The Black Phone is meaningful, scary, thrilling, and full of powerful performances.
reviews.author: Alan Cerny

reviews.text: The Black Phone expands on a short story in ways that feel very true to the source material while significantly enhancing its theatrical appeal.
reviews.author: John DeFore

reviews.text: A film with a bleak yet entertaining reminder that horror is omnipresent, but sometimes you can find a lifeline in the darkest of hours if you just listen.
reviews.author: Marisa Mirabal

reviews.text: Hawke's performance is fearless. But it's Mason Thames' nuanced turn as Finney that keeps The Black Phone grounded when the more supernatural elements come calling.
reviews.author: Drew Tinnin

synopsis: Finney, a shy but clever 13-year-old boy, is abducted by a sadistic killer and trapped in a soundproof basement where screaming is of little use. When a disconnected phone on the wall begins to ring, Finney discovers that he can hear the voices of the killer's previous victims. And they are dead set on making sure that what happened to them doesn't happen to Finney.
